feature.name: ship-from-repo
feature.summary: Let an app developer with no Docker/CI knowledge ship a GitHub repo+branch to AKS (devsand) from a dedicated page: a trust-separated flux-config workflow builds with Paketo buildpacks, Wiz-scans, publishes semver+sha tags to private ACR, and chains the existing flux-config config PR so a preview URL appears, with end-to-end status, logs, authorization and audit and no database.

acceptance_criteria: [FR-001] The Ship from Repo page (PageId 'ship' plus home card 'Ship an app from GitHub') is reachable only when authenticated and when at least one environment has features.shipFromRepo true; AKSDeployPage.vue and AKSInstalledAppsPage.vue are unchanged.

[FR-001/FR-016] Repo and branch lists contain only repositories in allowlisted orgs that both the requesting user and the Code App can read, excluding forks; inaccessible repos give an identical generic 'repo not accessible' answer.

[FR-002] POST /api/ship rejects (400) any environment lacking features.shipFromRepo and any invalid repo, branch, app, namespace, teamLabel, port, healthPath or bump; invalid input dispatches nothing.

[FR-003] POST /api/ship returns 202 with a server-minted UUIDv7 correlationId and dispatches ship-from-repo.yaml exactly once; triggered_by, triggered_by_oid and requester_github_login are set server-side and any such values in the body are discarded; per-user (<=3 active, <=6/h) and global (<=10 active, <=12/h) caps return 429 PLATFORM_RATE_LIMITED.

[FR-004/NFR-005] User code runs only in the GitHub-hosted build job (permissions {}, no secrets, no OIDC, no environment); prepare, scan and publish never execute repo content; the hostile-repo negative matrix passes.

[FR-005] Tags are exactly X.Y.Z (first ship 0.1.0, default patch bump on the highest semver tag, minor/major supported) plus sha-<7-char sha>; latest is never pushed; version is computed only inside the serialized publish section.

[FR-006] An image is pushed only when wizcli (policy e8ef1254-673e-4761-9e85-303ff6a37f17) exits 0 AND the structured JSON output's policy verdict (parsed with jq, never a substring of human-readable output) is pass, for the exact tar later pushed (SHA-256 equal); Wiz, Key Vault, missing verdict or unparsable JSON fail closed (SECURITY_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE); a hostile image whose text contains 'Scan results: PASSED' plus a blocking finding yields SECURITY_GATE_FAILED.

[FR-007] publish pushes selfserve/<app>:X.Y.Z and :sha-<short> to the ship registry via OIDC with push target restricted to selfserve/<validated-app> by a code-enforced allowlist checked before any registry call (anything else, incl. githubrunner/*, is rejected with PUBLISH_FAILED; WT-09b guard test; registry-wide AcrPush on the identity is the accepted R-A7, ABAC = post-pilot HO-3), overwrites provenance labels and sets ENV PORT, locks new tags, never overwrites a tag and leaves no unlocked partial tag after cancellation.

[FR-008] The same workflow dispatches generate-webapp-config.yaml (kv_secrets, env_vars, secret_env_vars, workload_identity_grants all []), waits for it inside the serialized section, resolves PR auto/gen-<env>-<app>, and the resulting PR triggers preview-on-pr; no downgrade of image_tag; post-merge ships skip config; CONFIG_PR_FAILED can be retried config-only.
[FR-009] Build logs are proxied, redacted server-side, incremental by offset, fetched only while the panel is open, capped at 5 MB in view and downloadable.

[FR-010] A preview URL pr-<N>-<app>.<suffix> is shown only after the PR number is known and only when SHIP_PREVIEW_HOSTS has an entry for the environment (no default domain); otherwise preview.state is not_configured and only the PR link is shown.
[FR-011] Every failed ship ends in exactly one of the 16 stable failure codes with a static plain-language message, next step and retry class; no stack traces, tokens or secrets are exposed.

[FR-012] Re-ship before merge updates the same PR and preview URL with a higher X.Y.Z; after merge it publishes only and Flux rolls it out; changed port/healthPath for a merged app are ignored server-side and reported in settingsIgnored.

[FR-013] Status resolves by correlationId (a UUIDv7 whose timestamp bounds the run search to <=3 GitHub calls at any age within retention while the DD-14 start cap holds (the window holds every ship-from-repo run in it), no client hint) beyond the legacy 10-run/60-minute window, is composed as a fold over all runs of the ID (a config_only retry keeps version/sha/digest/scan from the image-bearing run and never shows build/scan as skipped), polls every 15 s with single-flight caching, shows 7 internal stages mapped to the labels Build, Security check, Publish, Review PR, Preview; status and logs are readable by the starter (Entra oid), an authorized repo reader, or platform members, while cancel and retry are limited to the starter or platform members.

[FR-013] GET /api/aks-status-by-correlation/:correlationId requires authentication and applies an ownership rule that compares the sanitised by= (or the 'Triggered by:' job-log fallback for runs without by=) with the sanitised caller e-mail on both sides, so owners of existing AKS-page deploys (mixed-case or apostrophe e-mails, in-flight pre-change runs, BYO-image runs) are never 403'd; non-owners are 403'd; its success body shape is unchanged.

[FR-014] Every dispatched ship leaves a GitHub-resident record (run-name, trusted annotations, job summary, flux-config PR, ACR labels) retrievable by correlationId; pre-dispatch rejections appear only in API logs.

[FR-015] Recent ships are stored in localStorage under ship.recent.v1.<oid> (20 newest, no tokens, schema-validated on read, cleared on logout), refreshed only when non-terminal, with 403/404/error/empty states.

[FR-016] With no verified GitHub login mapping (provider 'none') every ship fails closed with REPO_NOT_ACCESSIBLE and hint IDENTITY_NOT_LINKED; a second source repo shipping an existing app name is rejected with APP_OWNED_BY_OTHER and cannot push to selfserve/<app>.
[Round-4 advisory] The page defines and tests states for loading, load error, no environment enabled (S1) and account not linked (S2); localStorage entries are cleared on sign-out.

[NFR-011] A ship uses at most ~200 GitHub API calls (including one config retry) and the platform sustains at most 12 ship starts per hour; N viewers of one ship cause one upstream status call per refresh.

[NFR-005/B-2] A ship.result annotation is accepted only as exactly one base64url payload per expected stage tag per trusted job (prepare: 1, scan: 1, publish job: publish + config in mode=full, config only in mode=config_only) emitted by emit-result.sh, with cid/runId/runAttempt/stage equal to the resolved run and ok:true only when the step group behind that stage (matched by exact step names) and the stage's Emit step concluded success (prepare/scan job; Publish: guard|verify image|version|push steps 1-4; Config PR: decide|guard|dispatch|wait steps 6-9; a skipped step never counts as success); text printed by trusted jobs (repo, clone errors, Wiz output) containing '::notice title=ship.result::' is inert (::stop-commands::) and can never become a decision.

[NFR-005/B-3] Every step on ubuntu-latest that handles attacker-controlled bytes (clone, tar, image-tar validation, crane) runs under ship-sandbox.sh (env -i, HOME override, no git global/system config, https-only, token via GIT_ASKPASS file) so canary ARM_CLIENT_SECRET, GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY and SSH key never appear in its environment, output or artifacts; the image tar is structurally validated before Wiz and before crane; prepare uses the existing Code App for a single-repo contents:read + metadata:read short-lived token (decided H-9, 2026-10-22); R-A6 accepted.

[Phase-1 gates/B-8] Every verification gate V-1..V-12 has a measurable pass criterion, evidence, decider, blocked phase and on-fail spec delta; the watchdog cancel side effect is off by default until V-4 passes; features.shipFromRepo cannot be enabled until every G-FLAG gate is PASS.

user_stories.as: App Developer with limited platform knowledge (Sam)
user_stories.i_want: to pick my GitHub repo and branch, press Ship, and get a preview URL without writing a Dockerfile or CI file
user_stories.so_that: I can try my app on AKS without platform-team help
acceptance_criteria: Only repos I can read appear; default view shows repo, branch, app name, environment and a Ship button with Advanced collapsed (AC-001-1..8, AC-002-*).
After Ship I see Build, Security check, Publish, Review PR, Preview progress and, on success, Version, PR link and preview URL (AC-013-1, AC-013-4, AC-010-*).
If anything fails I see a plain-language reason, next step and a Retry that is safe for that failure class (AC-011-*).

user_stories.i_want: to click Ship new version after I push code, and understand my changes are not auto-deployed
user_stories.so_that: iterations update the same PR and preview, and merged apps roll out via Flux, with no CI in my repo
acceptance_criteria: Re-ship before merge yields the same PR number and preview URL with a higher X.Y.Z (AC-012-1).
Re-ship after merge publishes only and says the version will roll out automatically; port/health path are read-only and enforced server-side (AC-012-2, AC-012-3).
Ship new version pre-fills repo, branch, app and settings from the previous ship, falling back to repo/branch/app (AC-012-6).

user_stories.i_want: to return to earlier ships from the same browser
user_stories.so_that: I can reopen results, PR state and Ship new version without searching GitHub
acceptance_criteria: Recent ships lists app, branch, start time and status; only non-terminal entries refresh (AC-015-1, AC-015-2).
Failed refresh, 403/404 and empty states are shown as specified and signing out clears the list (AC-015-3, Round-4 advisory).

user_stories.i_want: every pushed image to be scanned, traceable to a commit and requester, and promoted only through the flux-config PR
user_stories.so_that: untrusted code never reaches ACR or Flux without a gate and review
acceptance_criteria: Build runs only on a throwaway GitHub-hosted VM with no credentials; scanned tar SHA-256 equals pushed tar (AC-004-7, AC-006-1, AC-007-2).
Images carry sha-<short> and OCI labels set by the trusted job; no auto-merge is requested (AC-007-3, AC-008-4).
A different source repo cannot take over an existing app name (AC-016-3, AC-016-5).

user_stories.i_want: to read status and logs of any ship by correlationId and to see why runners or scans failed
user_stories.so_that: I can support users without GitHub access to flux-config
acceptance_criteria: Platform role/group membership (configured) grants status/log access; others get 403 and unknown runs 404 (AC-013-6).
Failure panels expose correlation ID and a copy-details payload (AC-011-8).

flows.name: Ship a repo (happy path)
steps: Step 1: Browser GET /api/ship/config and /api/environments; page enters S3 when identity linked and >=1 ship environment
Step 2: User picks repo (user ∩ App list) and branch; GET /api/ship/apps/:env/:app gives advisory ownership/app state
Step 3: POST /api/ship validates, checks flag, identity link, requester permission, app state, ownership, per-user and global caps; mints UUIDv7 correlationId
Step 4: Backend dispatches ship-from-repo.yaml once with Infrastructure App and returns 202; browser stores a Recent ships entry and starts 15 s polling
Step 5: prepare (ubuntu-latest, Code App single-repo token, steps run under ship-sandbox.sh) re-validates, re-checks requester access and ownership, pins SHA, uploads source without .git
Step 6: build (GitHub-hosted, untrusted) runs pack with digest-pinned Paketo builder, linux/amd64, exports image tar
Step 7: scan validates the tar structure, runs wizcli with policy e8ef1254 and passes only on exit 0 AND a jq-parsed JSON policy verdict of pass; emits tar SHA-256

Step 8: publish (serialized ship-<app>) re-validates the tar structure, verifies tar hash and ownership, computes X.Y.Z, pushes staging (token scoped to selfserve/*), mutates labels+PORT, tags X.Y.Z and sha-<short>, locks, cleans staging
Step 9: publish dispatches generate-webapp-config.yaml and polls (10 s, <=10 min, 3-min early signal); PR auto/gen-<env>-<app> opens via SVC_GITHUB_TOKEN so preview-on-pr runs; PR resolved by branch
Step 10: status endpoint folds all runs of the ID: 7 stages from jobs + validated trusted annotations + PR; UI shows Version, PR link and preview URL (if SHIP_PREVIEW_HOSTS configured)

Step 2: POST /api/ship determines appState; for merged apps changed port/healthPath are ignored and effective values substituted, response lists settingsIgnored
Step 3: Workflow builds, scans, publishes next patch under the same ship-<app> group (second concurrent ship queues)

flows.name: Status, logs, cancel, retry
steps: Step 1: GET status derives the search window from the UUIDv7 timestamp, lists runs of that window (<=3 pages while the DD-14 start cap holds; no early stop inside the retry window; metric ship_run_lookup_pages), caches the run set, authorizes read for (a) starter oid, (b) repo reader, (c) platform member; mutations only (a) or (c)

Step 2: One jobs-list call per active run derives stages; completed trusted jobs' annotations are validated once and cached; the status is folded over all runs (image-bearing run for version/digest/stages, newest run for state/failure/PR); PR read by branch after publish
Step 3: Logs are fetched only while panel is open, redacted per line, served by offset
Step 4: Cancel allowed only before publish starts (starter or platform member); retry-config-pr dispatches mode=config_only with the same correlation id, origin_run_id and retry_by

error_paths.error: run not found, expired, or timestamp out of window
error_paths.handling: 404 NOT_FOUND (state queued when the ID is < 3 min old); out-of-window IDs cost 0 GitHub calls

error_paths.error: trusted job queued >10 min on ubuntu-latest and not concurrency-blocked
error_paths.handling: RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE reported (report-only); the still-queued prepare is cancelled once only when SHIP_WATCHDOG_CANCEL_ENABLED (V-4 passed) and the viewer is starter/platform

error_paths.error: annotation fails consumer validation (duplicate, wrong cid/runId, bad encoding, ok:true on failed job)
error_paths.handling: stage result discarded, failure UNKNOWN, never success; metric ship_annotation_rejected

flows.name: Identity not linked (OQ-13 unresolved)
steps: Step 1: GET /api/ship/config returns identity.state='unlinked' (provider none)
Step 2: UI shows S2 notice and disables the form; Recent ships remain visible
Step 3: Any direct POST /api/ship returns 403 REPO_NOT_ACCESSIBLE with hint IDENTITY_NOT_LINKED and dispatches nothing

error_scenarios.handling: Retry reads with backoff (3 attempts); guard extends cache TTL; ship triggers fail PLATFORM_RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After
error_scenarios.user_message: GitHub is busy right now. Try again in a minute.
error_scenarios.logging: github_api_call metric with status_code and correlationId

error_scenarios.handling: Throw immediately, 500 UNKNOWN without detail; per-app failure isolated (Code App down does not break status reads)

error_scenarios.handling: scan fails closed, nothing pushed
error_scenarios.user_message: Security scanning is unavailable; nothing was published. Retry later.

error_scenarios.scenario: Security gate failed
error_scenarios.handling: SECURITY_GATE_FAILED with severity counts and top findings; nothing pushed; policy not overridable
error_scenarios.user_message: Security check failed; nothing was published. Fix the listed packages and ship again.

error_scenarios.scenario: Annotation channel unreadable (V-3) or forged/invalid
error_scenarios.handling: Artifact fallback if V-3 fails; any annotation failing validation (duplicate, wrong cid/runId/runAttempt/stage, bad encoding, ok:true on a failed job) is discarded and the stage fails UNKNOWN, never a false success
error_scenarios.user_message: We couldn't read the result. Copy details for the platform team.
error_scenarios.logging: warn ship_annotation_rejected{reason} with jobId and ship correlationId

error_scenarios.scenario: Hostile text in repo, clone error, or scanner output containing workflow commands
error_scenarios.handling: Printed only via emit-untrusted.sh inside ::stop-commands::<random>; one emit-result.sh annotation per stage tag; consumer requires exactly one per expected stage tag per job
error_scenarios.user_message: none (no user-visible effect)
error_scenarios.logging: ship_annotation_rejected if a duplicate is observed

error_scenarios.scenario: Runner pool saturated (publish waiting on a config run that needs the same pool)
error_scenarios.handling: Config wait polls 10 s and signals configQueued after 3 min; timeout 10 min => CONFIG_PR_FAILED hint runner busy, retry via config_only; global active cap keeps ships <= pool - 2
error_scenarios.user_message: Waiting for a platform runner; you can retry PR creation if this fails.

error_scenarios.scenario: Config PR step failed or PR not found
error_scenarios.handling: CONFIG_PR_FAILED, image remains locked in ACR, Retry PR creation runs mode=config_only without rebuild (same ID, origin_run_id, within 24 h; status folds the retry with the original run)
error_scenarios.user_message: Your image was published but the review PR couldn't be opened. Retry PR creation.

error_scenarios.scenario: Namespace collision or app already exists in flux-config config run
error_scenarios.handling: Surfaces as CONFIG_PR_FAILED with hint from static catalogue
error_scenarios.user_message: That namespace or app is already in use. Choose another namespace.

error_scenarios.scenario: Runner queue > 10 min (ubuntu-latest)
error_scenarios.handling: RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE reported by the resolver (report-only; terminal=false while the run is still queued); cancel side effect only when SHIP_WATCHDOG_CANCEL_ENABLED (after V-4), only for a never-started prepare, only for starter/platform viewer, once; otherwise the UI's Retry first calls the user-initiated cancel
error_scenarios.user_message: The platform runners are busy. Retry, or contact the platform team.

error_scenarios.scenario: Per-user or global start/active cap reached
error_scenarios.handling: 429 PLATFORM_RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After and details.limit in {user_active,user_hourly,global_active,global_hourly,github}
error_scenarios.user_message: Too many ships are running right now. Try again shortly.

error_scenarios.scenario: Workflow ref equals the default branch without SHIP_ALLOW_DEFAULT_REF
error_scenarios.handling: POST /api/ship refuses to dispatch (503 unavailable); config misconfiguration fails closed
error_scenarios.user_message: Ship from Repo is temporarily unavailable.
error_scenarios.logging: error with config key name only

error_scenarios.scenario: Third simultaneous ship of one app
error_scenarios.handling: Pending publish displaced and cancelled by GitHub; derived SUPERSEDED (or CANCELLED if cancel was requested)
error_scenarios.user_message: A newer ship replaced this one. Ship again.

error_scenarios.scenario: Cancel after publish started
error_scenarios.handling: 409 CANCEL_NOT_ALLOWED; publish critical section traps INT/TERM and an always() step locks any new tag
error_scenarios.user_message: You can't cancel once publishing has started.

error_scenarios.handling: preview.state=not_configured; PR link shown, no URL constructed

jobs.if: mode == full; needs prepare; no secrets.*, no OIDC, no cache

jobs.trust: no user code executed (tar structure validation + parse only)
trusted, concurrency group ship-<app>, cancel-in-progress false; attacker-byte steps run under ship-sandbox.sh
jobs.environment: ship-publish (OIDC identity ship-publish, registry AcrPush on exampleregistry; push target limited to selfserve/<validated-app> by the code-enforced allowlist, DD-16)

step_groups.Publish: work steps: exact step names Publish: guard, Publish: verify image, Publish: version, Publish: push (steps 1-4); matched by exact name, never by prefix (N3-A4); Publish: cleanup (step 5, if: always(), continue-on-error: true) is excluded and its failure does not skip steps 6-9 (N3-A2)
step_groups.Config PR: work steps: exact step names Config PR: decide, Config PR: guard, Config PR: dispatch, Config PR: wait (steps 6-9); fail-fast, no continue-on-error; steps 7-9 are never if:-skipped (they run as no-ops and exit 0 on skip_config) because a skipped step concludes skipped, not success (N3-A3)
step_groups.Emit: publish: separate emit step, if: always() && mode == full, exactly one publish-stage annotation; skipped in config_only
step_groups.Emit: config: separate emit step, always(), exactly one config-stage annotation
step_groups.mode_config_only: steps that run: Publish: guard (ship-publish OIDC login, read-only use through the guarded registry function), Publish: cleanup (no-op), Config PR: decide/guard/dispatch/wait, Emit: config; steps 2-4 and Emit: publish are if: mode == full (skipped, not evaluated) (N3-A3)
step_groups.validity: ok:true for stage publish needs Publish: steps 1-4 success and Emit: publish success; for stage config needs Config PR: steps 6-9 success and Emit: config success; only the conclusion success counts (skipped does not); the publish job conclusion is not consulted (N-1, N3-A3, N3-A4)

trust_rules: Trusted-to-trusted data flows use job outputs only, never artifacts
The only artifact consumed by a trusted job is ship-image after SHA-256 equality with needs.scan.outputs.tar_sha256 and structural validation by validate-image-tar.mjs (in scan and again in publish)
Build annotations/log text are display hints only

Trusted-job logs are untrusted text: untrusted text is printed only via emit-untrusted.sh (::stop-commands::<random>); ship.result is emitted only by emit-result.sh (jq -c, base64url), exactly once per expected stage tag per trusted job (publish job: publish and config; separate Emit steps)
Security verdicts come from wizcli exit status AND jq-parsed JSON output, never from human-readable text

Z2 hygiene: step-level secrets only; ship-sandbox.sh (env -i, HOME override, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM=/dev/null, https-only, GIT_ASKPASS file, no SSH) for clone/tar/validate/crane; the existing Code App key is held only in the ship-prepare environment and exposed only to the single token-minting step (DD-15; R-A6 accepted by the product owner for the devsand pilot, H-9 decided 2026-10-22)
All inputs passed via env: and quoted; whitelists (incl. reserved-namespace denylist) re-validated in every job
Tools (pack, crane, wizcli) pinned by version and checksum; actions pinned by commit SHA; builder pinned by digest

ship-publish's push target is limited to selfserve/<validated-app> by a code-enforced allowlist checked before any registry call (host = $SHIP_REGISTRY, repository exactly selfserve/<validated-app>, tag X.Y.Z|sha-<7>|_stg-<cid8>); anything else (incl. githubrunner/*) is rejected with PUBLISH_FAILED and nothing is sent (WT-09b guard test). The identity itself has registry-wide AcrPush: residual risk R-A7 accepted by the product owner for the devsand pilot (H-10, 2026-10-22); ABAC is post-pilot HO-3

DECIDED by the product owner 2026-10-22 (H-9): prepare reuses the existing Code App (code-deployment GitHub App) for repo read and permission checks - installation token scoped to the single requested repo via repositories[], permissions contents:read + metadata:read only, short-lived, revoked in always(); the App ID/key are step-level secrets SHIP_CODE_APP_ID/SHIP_CODE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY of environment ship-prepare (minting step only); no dedicated Ship Reader App. Residual risk R-A6 (ambient credentials on ubuntu-latest and the Code App key held in an flux-config environment) is explicitly ACCEPTED by the product owner for the devsand pilot; compensating control = the Z2 hygiene wrapper (env -i, GIT_CONFIG_*=/dev/null, GIT_ASKPASS file, tar validation; WT-04b/V-12). Dedicated Ship Reader App (HO-1) and dedicated runner group/uid separation (HO-2) are post-pilot hardening options, not Phase-1 blockers

DECIDED by the product owner 2026-10-22 (H-10): the existing registry exampleregistry is used (no separate registry); the push target in publish is limited to selfserve/<validated-app> by a code-enforced allowlist evaluated before any registry call (host = $SHIP_REGISTRY; repository exactly selfserve/<validated-app>; tag X.Y.Z|sha-<7>|_stg-<cid8>; anything else rejected with PUBLISH_FAILED); negative test WT-09b retained as a guard test (no live probe against githubrunner/*); V-8 = verify the code guard + record ABAC status. Residual risk R-A7 (ship-publish OIDC identity has registry-wide AcrPush) is explicitly ACCEPTED by the product owner for the devsand pilot. Fallback ladder (post-pilot, none blocks Phase 1): ACR repository-scoped ABAC selfserve/* (recommended, HO-3), else separate registry (HO-3b), optionally job_workflow_ref pin (HO-4)

Ship ID is a server-minted UUIDv7 (uuid v11 v7(); same-millisecond IDs differ via the random tail); its timestamp derives the run-search window (window holds every ship-from-repo run in [t-3 min, t+retry window+1 h] (start t-3 min = ASM-13 skew 2 min + dispatch/queue latency, N3-A1), so <=3 pages is bounded by the DD-14 start cap); no since hint; future-timestamp 404 (> now + 2 min) is valid only under ASM-13 (clock skew <= 2 min)
ShipStatus is a fold over all runs of the ID: stages/version/digest from the image-bearing run, state/failure/PR from the newest run; one run-name template/regex/input name (mode, retry_by)

Product-owner decisions 2026-10-22 (decision log; keep the initial implementation simple, reuse what exists, add no infrastructure): H-9 decided (DD-15), H-10 decided (DD-16), R-A6/R-A7 accepted for the devsand pilot. Identity count: the ship-prepare OIDC identity is KEPT (three identities remain) because AC-016-3 requires the ownership-label read in prepare before any build; reusing ship-publish there would put a registry-write credential in the job that clones attacker-controlled repo bytes, OIDC subjects are per GitHub environment so prepare cannot borrow ship-scan (and giving ship-scan registry rights would widen the Z3 job that parses the untrusted tar), and dropping the prepare check in favour of publish step 3 alone changes AC-016-3 (needs a PM decision). Post-pilot hardening options (documented, not blockers): HO-1 dedicated Ship Reader App, HO-2 dedicated runner group/uid separation, HO-3 ACR repository-scoped ABAC (HO-3b separate registry), HO-4 job_workflow_ref pin
